name: DNB Bank ASA
reason: Dominant Norwegian bank but earnings are at the rate-cycle peak (adjusted EPS NOK 28.4 in 2025 = 0.97x the 10-year max vs 15.65 in 2021) with 12.5% average ROE and consensus of -7.3% FY1 and +7.6%/+3.7% FY2-FY3 (LTG 3.9%), so there is no NIM-independent route to 7% growth.

name: AIB Group plc
reason: Irish bank whose EPS of EUR 0.93 (2025) is only back to 2015's 0.53 path after a 2020 loss, with 8.1% average ROE showing it was not best-in-class at zero rates; current profits are peak-NIM earnings (consensus -3.6% FY1).

name: Banco de Sabadell SA
reason: Spanish bank with 5.8% 10-year average ROE and flat revenue (0.1%/yr) whose EPS of EUR 0.28 sits at a rate-driven peak after a 2020 loss; ordinary franchise with no through-cycle record.

name: SpareBank 1 SMN
reason: Regional Norwegian savings bank with 9.0% average ROE at peak earnings (EPS NOK 19.11 = 10-year max), consensus of -6.2% FY1 and LTG of 2%, and a rising share count (+1.1%/yr); solid but cheap-but-ordinary.

name: Alerion Clean Power S.p.A.
reason: Italian wind generator whose earnings track merchant power prices and incentives: EBIT margin is at the 91st percentile of its history (51.7% vs 38% average), FCF is negative, acquisitions/capex run at 2.6x FCF and net debt/EBITDA is 4.0x.

name: Argan
reason: French logistics REIT whose FFO/share grew only 4.8%/yr over 5 years to EUR 6.00 while shares rose 6.1%/yr and net debt/EBITDA is 8.8x, so growth is funded by leverage and issuance; consensus FY1 -11%.

name: MONTEA NV
reason: Belgian logistics REIT with a steady FFO/share record (EUR 2.15 to 4.96, 8.7%/yr) but it was built on 9.2%/yr share issuance and 9.5x net debt/EBITDA, so growth depends on capital markets and leverage; LTG is 5.4%.

name: Jyske Bank A/S
reason: Danish bank whose EPS spiked with rates to DKK 123.9 (2023) and has already fallen to 85.5 (0.69x the peak), with 9.4% average ROE and a 2020 EPS drop of -47%; earnings are set by the rate cycle.

name: permanent tsb Group Holdings PLC
reason: State-controlled Irish mortgage bank with 0.9% 10-year average ROE, losses in 2015, 2020 and 2021, EPS of EUR 0.19 at 0.43x its 2022 peak, and adjusted EPS averaging 92% above GAAP.

name: A2A S.p.A.
reason: Municipally controlled Italian multi-utility whose EPS (EUR 0.22, down 16% in 2025) swings with power and gas prices and whose consensus growth is only 2.3%/5.2% for FY2-FY3, below the 7% bar.

name: CaixaBank SA
reason: Spain's largest retail bank with EPS of EUR 0.83 at the 10-year high after the Bankia merger and rate rises, but zero-rate-era EPS was flat (0.19 in 2016 to 0.28 in 2021) and 10-year average ROE is 9.8%, so it fails the through-cycle best-in-class test; the foundation and the state's FROB hold large stakes.

name: Bank Handlowy w Warszawie S.A.
reason: Citi's Polish subsidiary whose EPS went from PLN 2.00 (2020) to 17.36 (2023) purely on rates and is now falling (13.10 in 2025, consensus -17.5% FY1, LTG 2.6%), with the parent exiting retail banking.

name: Julius Baer Gruppe AG
reason: Swiss private bank whose adjusted EPS grew only 2.8%/yr over 10 years (CHF 3.25 to 4.27) and fell 56% in 2023 on the Signa credit losses; earnings depend on AUM, market levels and trading activity.

name: Warehouses De Pauw SA
reason: Well-run logistics REIT with FFO/share up every year (EUR 0.71 to 1.53) but the growth was funded by 6.0%/yr share issuance and 8.4x net debt/EBITDA, and consensus is only 5-7% (LTG 5.1%), below the 7% bar.

name: XTB Spolka Akcyjna
reason: Fast-growing Polish online broker (36% average ROE, net cash, revenue +22.7%/yr) but CFD trading income is set by market volatility, so EPS swings widely (PLN 0.49 in 2019, 6.53 in 2022, 5.48 in 2025 with EBIT margin from 67% to 37%) and leverage-product regulation is a live risk.

name: Melrose Industries PLC
reason: Now a pure aerospace group (GKN Aerospace) after its buy-improve-sell history, with acquisitions at 2.8x FCF, 18%/yr share-count growth over 10 years and average ROIC of -1.4%; the EBIT margin is at its 10-year high (11.0%), so the 30%/21% consensus growth rests on an untested 2-year record.

name: thyssenkrupp AG
reason: Steel-heavy conglomerate with losses in 5 of the last 8 years, an average EBIT margin of -1.1%, revenue shrinking 2.6%/yr and a 10-year average ROE of -11.6%; it fails the forecastability and returns tests.

name: ASR Nederland N.V.
reason: Dutch insurer whose growth came from the Aegon NL acquisition (shares +4.3%/yr), with operating EPS of EUR 5.74 at a high, a 42% average adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and consensus of only +0.8%/+5.2% for FY2-FY3 (LTG 3%).

name: SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge
reason: Northern Norwegian savings bank at peak EPS (NOK 15.28) with 8.2% 10-year average ROE, consensus of -7.8% FY1 and LTG of 1%; ordinary regional lender.

name: Elopak ASA
reason: Distant third in liquid-food cartons behind Tetra Pak and SIG, with EPS of EUR 0.23 (2025) only modestly above 0.19 (2020), 1 of 5 years with growth of 7% or more, a thin 9.1% EBIT margin at the 83rd percentile of its short history and adjusted EPS 20% above GAAP; cheap-but-ordinary.
